PARENT vs CHILD (the point of this table): the S2 File carries a SEPARATE Parent's Protocol version of this questionnaire and it is that version that ships here. (1) The instructions are entirely different -- the parents' are a self-administered written rubric ('We have collected some possible explanations ... 1 means strongly disagree and 4 means strongly agree'), not the child protocol's bag-of-pictures script with its two warm-up examples. (2) The response anchors differ and were NOT inherited from the child form: the four-expressive-faces card (1 a lot / 2 a little disagreement, 3 a little / 4 a lot agreement) is described in the Measures section as what CHILDREN pointed to, and the parent protocol labels only its two endpoints, so option_text is populated at resp 1 ('strongly disagree') and resp 4 ('strongly agree') only. (3) All eleven statements were diffed against the child form character by character: exactly one differs, statement (viii), which reads 'his body does not function well and the world makes him things difficult' for parents against '...makes him think it is difficult' for children; the parent reading is shipped verbatim, odd grammar included. (4) The four stimulus descriptions in section_prompt are taken from the PARENT protocol's own open-ended section, where (iii) reads 'Paolo is autistic and he does not understand what others say' against the child protocol's 'and does not understand'. (5) Same masculine-only limitation as the child table: the codebook prints only the masculine set although Maria (SD) and Elena (ND) were administered in feminine form, which no source publishes -- see public_note.
